extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers studying algebraic geometry and homological algebra (readers of Vakil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: Working through Vakil's textbook material and exercises on blow-ups, resolution of singularities, deformation to the normal cone, Picard/canonical-line-bundle behavior under blow-ups, and the introduction to Tor and derived functors. Includes definitions, computations, and exercises that show how these constructions behave.

rubrics_metrics.name: de_Jong_alteration_principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than producing a birational proper map X from something regular, de Jong’s Alteration Theorem produces a proper map from something regular that is generically finite (and the corresponding extension of function fields is separable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is often 'good enough' for applications where a true resolution (birational proper map) is not available; note characteristic issues (Hironaka in char 0 vs alterations in positive characteristic). The statement is used as a practical substitute for full resolution in many arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: caution_blowing_up_nonreduced_subschemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Blowing up a nonreduced subscheme of a regular scheme can give you something singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.G: Example: the blow up of the closed subscheme V(y, x^2) in Spec k[x,y] = A^2 yields an A1 surface singularity. Use explicit local equations to verify the singularity; takeaway: nonreduced centers can create singularities even when ambient is regular.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolving_tacnode_by_specific_blow_up
rubrics_metrics.description: The tacnode y^2 = x^4 can be desingularized in a single step by blowing up the ideal (y, x^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.H: Compare with a two-step resolution as in earlier exercises; choose the correct center (here (y,x^2)) to achieve a single-step resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: unexpected_blow_up_may_resolve_singularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Blowing up a codimension 1 locus that is not an effective Cartier divisor can nevertheless produce a regular blow-up and resolve singularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.I: Example: Y the cone x^2 + y^2 = z^2 and X the line x=0, y=z on Y; Bl_X Y is regular and is an isomorphism away from the cone point because X is Cartier away from that point. Moral: the local Cartier property can control where blow-up alters the space.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiplicity_of_function_at_regular_point
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is a function on a locally Noetherian scheme X, its multiplicity at a regular point p is the largest m such that f lies in the mth power of the maximal ideal of O_{X,p}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.7: Use this to detect singularities: V(f) is singular at p iff multiplicity m > 1. Compute multiplicity via local equations; multiplicity is an invariant used throughout blow-up calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiplicity_of_exceptional_divisor_in_total_transform
rubrics_metrics.description: When blowing up the origin in A^n, the multiplicity of the exceptional divisor in the total transform of a subscheme Z is the smallest multiplicity (at the origin) of a defining equation of Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.J: For nodal and cuspidal curves the exceptional divisor appears with multiplicity 2. Use explicit local defining equations to compute multiplicities and compare proper vs. total transform.

rubrics_metrics.name: blow_ups_resolve_base_locus_of_rational_map
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a scheme Y, an invertible sheaf L and sections s0,...,sn (a linear series), blowing up the base locus X cut out by s0=...=sn=0 resolves the rational map to P^n: the rational map extends uniquely to a morphism Bl_X Y -> P^n corresponding to the invertible sheaf (β^* L)(-E_{X/Y}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.L: To prove, work locally where L is trivial; uniqueness may use earlier exercises. Conceptual remark: blowing up makes the base locus an effective Cartier divisor EXY which can be 'divided out' from the pulled-back sections to obtain a base-point-free linear series.

rubrics_metrics.name: interpretation_base_locus_as_effective_cartier_divisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the blow-up Bl_X Y the base locus pulls back to the exceptional divisor EXY, which is an effective Cartier divisor; because EXY is locally a non-zerodivisor one can divide the pulled-back sections by EXY to remove the base locus and obtain a base-point-free series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 22.4.9(ii): This explains why blowing up is the minimal 'modification' to remove base points. If X is already Cartier one can remove base locus by dividing out X without blow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: graph_of_rational_map_as_blow_up
rubrics_metrics.description: For sections s0,...,sn of an invertible sheaf on integral scheme X, the graph of the rational map φ: X --> P^n is isomorphic to Bl_{V(s0,...,sn)} X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.M: The isomorphism is constructed without needing to work over a field; it identifies the graph with the blow-up along the base ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: small_resolution_definition_and_examples
rubrics_metrics.description: A small resolution is a resolution Y -> X such that the locus where fibers have dimension r has codimension greater than 2r. Small resolutions can differ (non-isomorphic) and lead to flops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.N and Remark 22.4.11: Example from cone over quadric: resolving by blowing up a base locus yields a small resolution whose exceptional fibre over cone point is P^1 (codimension 2). Different small resolutions can be related by Atiyah flop; be careful: small resolutions are not unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: weak_factorization_theorem_statement
rubrics_metrics.description: In characteristic 0, any two birational varieties X and Y may be related by a sequence of blow-ups and blow-downs along smooth subvarieties (Weak Factorization Theorem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 22.4.12: There exist intermediate varieties X_0,...,X_n with X_0 = X and X_n = Y and morphisms between adjacent Xi given by blow-ups of smooth centers. Reference Włodarczyk for proof; this is a structural theorem about birational geometry in char 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: picard_group_change_under_blow_up_of_point_on_surface
rubrics_metrics.description: For X a regular projective surface and β: Bl_p X -> X the blow-up at a k-point p with exceptional divisor E, one has a short exact sequence relating Picard groups and an isomorphism Pic(Bl_p X) ≅ Pic X ⊕ Z generated by O_E(-1); E is a (-1)-curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.O: Use exact sequences (14.2.8.1) and intersection theory to show β^* gives a section and γ is injective. This yields how Pic and N1 change under blowing up a point.

rubrics_metrics.name: pullback_formula_for_cartier_divisor_under_blow_up
rubrics_metrics.description: If D is an effective Cartier divisor (a curve) on X and mult_p D denotes its multiplicity at p, then for π: Bl_p X -> X the blow-up, π^* D = D^{pr} + (mult_p D) E as effective Cartier divisors, and π^* O_X(D) ≅ O_{Bl_p X}(D^{pr}) ⊗ O_{Bl_p X}(E)^{mult_p D}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.P: Verify by relating local equations: the product of local equation for proper transform and the mult_p(D)-th power of local equation for E equals local equation for π^*D. Useful concrete formula in computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: canonical_bundle_change_under_blow_up
rubrics_metrics.description: Under blowing up at a point in dimension n, the canonical bundle changes by adding the exceptional divisor with multiplicity (n-1): for instance in dimension 2, K_X ≅ (π^* K_Y)(E); generally K_X ≅ (β^* K_Y)((n-1)E) and if blowing up smooth subvariety Z of dimension m in Y^n then K_X ≅ (β^* K_Y)((n - m - 1)E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 22.4.14, 22.4.Q–S: Compute by pulling back a local generator of K_Y and checking vanishing order along the exceptional divisor; choose local coordinates (x,y,...) adapted to the center.

rubrics_metrics.name: dimensional_cohomology_vanishing_for_quasiprojective_schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a quasiprojective k-scheme of dimension d and F a quasicoherent sheaf on X, then H^i(X,F) = 0 for i > d; moreover a quasiprojective variety of dimension n can be covered by n+1 affine open subsets (using blow-ups and embeddings into projective variety).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.T and 22.4.15: Use closure in projective variety and blow-up of complement to arrange affine covers; link to Theorem 18.2.6 (dimensional cohomology vanishing for projective schemes). Note warning: not every variety can be covered by n+1 affines (non-quasiprojective counterexamples).

rubrics_metrics.name: deformation_to_the_normal_cone_construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The deformation to the normal cone: blowing up X×{0} inside Y×A^1 yields a flat family whose general fiber is Y and special fiber over 0 is the projective completion of the normal cone to X in Y; the special fiber is the scheme-theoretic union of Bl_X Y and the projective completion of the normal cone, intersecting along EXY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 22.4.U: Use the blow-up composition with projection to A^1 and identify fibers; this construction is central in modern intersection theory (Fulton-MacPherson) and used to degenerate intersections to the normal cone.

rubrics_metrics.name: tor_functors_definition_via_resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor^A_i(M,N) is defined by taking a free (or projective) resolution R -> N, tensoring with M to obtain M ⊗_A R and defining Tor_i^A(M,N) as the homology of this complex at the ith stage; Tor_0 ≅ M ⊗_A N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 23.1: Construction independent of choice of resolution via homotopy and lifting arguments; tensoring with M is right-exact so higher homology captures failure of exactness. Use explicit free resolutions built from generators to compute examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: long_exact_sequence_of_tor_and_horseshoe_construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a short exact sequence 0 -> N' -> N -> N'' -> 0, there is a long exact sequence of Tor_i^A(M, · ) relating Tor(M,N'), Tor(M,N), Tor(M,N'') and M ⊗_A (· ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 23.1.2 and the horseshoe construction (23.1.2.1): combine resolutions of N' and N'' to build a resolution of N (middle 'horseshoe' row), truncate, tensor with M and take homology to get the long exact sequence. Exercises verify details of lift choices and exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: flatness_characterized_by_vanishing_of_tor
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is flat iff Tor_i^A(M,N) = 0 for all i > 0 and all A-modules N (equivalently iff Tor_1^A(M,N) = 0 for all N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 23.1.D: Use that free/projective modules are flat and that vanishing of higher Tori detects exactness preservation under tensor. This is a key practical test for flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: derived_functors_general_definition
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a right-exact covariant functor on an abelian category with enough projectives, its left derived functors L_i F (i ≥ 0 with L_0 F = F) are defined by applying F to projective resolutions and taking homology; dually, for left-exact functors one defines right derived functors R^i F using injective resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 23.2.2: The abstract construction mirrors the Tor case. Assumptions needed: enough projectives/injectives in the category and that F behaves well on sums/products (additivity). Derived functors yield long exact sequences associated to short exact sequences in the source category.

rubrics_metrics.name: ext_functors_two_definitions_and_properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Ext^i_A(M,N) can be defined either as the right derived functors of Hom(·,N) applied to M (using projective resolutions) or as the right derived functors of Hom(M,·) applied to N (using injective resolutions); the two definitions agree and yield long exact sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 23.2.D/E and 23.3.B: Both approaches produce Ext and both associated long exact sequences are useful. If A is Noetherian and M,N finitely generated, Ext^i_A(M,N) is finitely generated. Use whichever resolution type is convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: category_has_enough_injectives_and_universal_delta_functor
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of a cohomological δ-functor abstracts derived functors: a collection of additive functors T^i with connecting morphisms δ^i producing long exact sequences for every short exact sequence and functoriality. If the category has enough injectives then the right derived functors R^i F form the (unique) universal δ-functor extending a left-exact functor F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 23.2.6–23.2.10: Universality can be checked by effaceability conditions; practical corollary: in abelian categories with enough injectives the derived functor construction yields canonical (universal) δ-functors. Exercises outline proofs and necessary lemmas (effaceable, monomorphism into J with vanishing higher T^i).

rubrics_metrics.name: horseshoe_and_lifting_maps_homotopy_independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Maps of resolutions lifting a given module map are homotopic, and homotopic maps induce the same map on homology; these facts guarantee independence of derived functor computations from the choice of resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crucial exercise 23.1.B and 23.1.A: The lifting argument uses freeness/projectivity and (implicitly) Choice; show homotopy of different lifts and use Exercise 23.1.A to prove induced maps on Tor or derived functor homology are independent of choices.
